rounds.panel_rationale: Both core lenses always on. completeness because the spec has 9 sections. feasibility and doctrine-compliance triggered by agent/marketplace-plugin design content; feasibility is the highest-value lens here because the spec restates an external platform contract and then builds a validator enforcing that restatement.

rejected.candidate: Purpose's 'Fifteen agent definitions' vs the 15-row table excluding the already-repaired fe-tester — present-tense 'declare' makes fifteen the post-fe-tester count.
'The contract' omits hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode from Permitted yet calls them silently ignored — a coherent three-way taxonomy, not a contradiction.
'Bash specifier form' says the question is avoided while Check V1 says to repeat with the colon form — the Resolution constrains what is written, not what is observed.
Delivery's PATCH rationale vs fix-auto shrinking from all-tools — 'altering it' refers to the intent, not the tool count.
Verification's expected-entry list omits four agents while instructing agent-by-agent comparison — the list is labelled expectations, not an exhaustive checklist.
Site counts across sections (9/1, ~10/~8, 'roughly eighteen') — all consistent.
Rows marked 'unchanged' could read as 'do not touch the file' while allowed-tools must still be deleted — the preceding sentence scopes 'unchanged' to the tools column.
Validator has no stated rule for mcp__ or ToolName(specifier) entries — 'Tool grants' forces acceptance of both forms.
be-tester uses bare mcp__postgres while web-auditor uses wildcards — 'Tool grants' sanctions both forms explicitly.
'exits zero on the repaired tree' may conflict with warnings the repaired tree still emits — warnings are defined as non-failing.
The canonical tool-name list is not enumerated — explicitly delegated to tools-reference as a dated constant.
TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList never resolve in background runs and the spec leaves them declared — explicitly decided and disclosed.
Whether the new workflow is a required merge check is unstated — branch-protection policy is ops, not spec design.
Frontmatter parsing shape for tools: is unspecified — implementation-plan detail, delegated to the existing script's structure.

be-tester and web-auditor agents declare skills: but no Skill tool — the repo's superutils agents demonstrate skills are preloaded without the Skill tool; fix-auto differs because it has no skills: key.
Agent may be unavailable to the web-auditor coordinator, itself a subagent — nesting defaults to three layers, nothing in the repo contradicts it.
feedback-analyzer carries a live colon-form Bash(git:*) the spec never repairs — its body never invokes Bash, and the validator's colon-form warning surfaces it anyway.
Trailing whitespace in 'model: opus ' would break hand-rolled parsing — implementation detail of the script, not a spec-level claim.
Item 4 (human gate / fail-closed TTY probe) — trigger absent: no headless autonomous mode is designed.
Item 6 (iteration/dispatch/time budgets) — met for what is designed; the repairs are one-off, not iterative.
Item 9 (provenance guard) — trigger absent: nothing in this spec auto-corrects.
Item 10 (durable sidecar) — trigger absent: no loop-critical state persists between validator runs.
Item 11 (scoped recoverable writes) — trigger fires and is met: one branch, one PR, explicit file list, nothing committed to master.
'No tools: field at all' warning is fail-open — the spec reasons the case explicitly and still surfaces it.

rounds.orchestrator_notes: SR-014 was surfaced by the SR-010(b) challenger during adjudication rather than by a panel lens, then confirmed by direct orchestrator evidence (grep of web-auditor.md lines 378/381/382/404). It is recorded as a finding rather than discarded on the formal ground that challengers return verdicts, not findings; silently dropping a verified defect is the exact behaviour the self-falsification rule forbids. Its lens is recorded as 'orchestrator' to keep panel attribution honest. Two knock-on edits flagged in the fixer's notes (the aged-constant residual risk still saying 'false errors' after SR-012 moved unrecognised names to warnings, and the Scope bullet not covering the four TaskOutput sites added by SR-014) were applied as orchestrator edits in the same batch, since both are direct consequences of approved fixes rather than new findings.

rounds.panel_rationale: Same lens set as round 1, fresh agent instances, reviewing the revised text with no knowledge of what round 1 changed. Withholding the change list is deliberate: telling the panel what was fixed would hand the verifier the exact target it grades.
rounds.orchestrator_notes: No round-2 finding from round 1 reappeared: all fourteen round-1 fixes held. The round-2 challenger quorum was SKIPPED by explicit user decision at the budget gate, trading adversarial confirmation for fix time. The nine applied round-2 fixes therefore rest on orchestrator evidence plus the user's batch approval, not on challenger survival — recorded here and in the report's Coverage section as the run's largest confidence gap. Four were confirmed by direct repository evidence before any edit: SR-020 (.gitignore:3 excludes CLAUDE.local.md and no tracked CLAUDE.md exists), SR-022 (ten run_in_background: true instructions survive a bare Task->Agent substitution), SR-018 (agent bodies hold exactly one mcp__ occurrence each, the allowed-tools line being deleted; the real references live in eight SKILL.md files), SR-021 (fe-tester ships wildcard-only). SR-019 was refuted on orchestrator evidence: the subagent docs state skills: injects listed skill content at startup and the Skill tool is needed only for skills not preloaded, demonstrated in-session by spec-reviewer agents that declare no Skill tool yet correctly applied lens-catalog. SR-023 through SR-029 were never dispatched to a challenger; the three majors are recorded unconfirmed rather than refuted, and block any claim of convergence. No round 3 ran, so the round-2 fixes were never re-reviewed by a fresh panel — the exact check that caught round 1's second-order defects.
